elaine_cs: FYI — onboarding account ClearNorth showing a latency SLO miss last week (p99 ~ 820ms, target 600ms). Renewal is coming up next month. Need comms + credit calc. Who can own?

maya_success: Onboarding progress is ~60%. They've hit two infra incidents in last 90d. CS playbook mentions offering a credit if we miss SLO twice in a quarter — want confirmation.

tom_platform: There's a metric slice on the SLO dashboard for ClearNorth: https://redwood.internal/dashboard/slo/clearnorth — it has p50/p95/p99 and incident annotations.

raj_reliability: I looked into the spike — correlated with model rollout on 2026-03-12. Autoscale policy didn't spin up fast enough due to an empty warm pool. Filed a short postmortem.

raj_reliability: Incident created: INC-2026-412, assigned to reliability. I'll attach the runbook and the scaling tweak we'll deploy.

ops_bot: Deploy bot: rollout/optimize-autoscale v2 deployed to staging at 2026-03-13T22:03Z :white_check_mark:

ben_engineer: I can run the credit numbers. Need their monthly invoice / committed spend. Also need minutes-of-degradation. Do we have the precise window?

elaine_cs: Thanks Ben — monthly ARR footprint for them is $540k (~$45k MRR). The SLO window: 2026-03-09 14:10 to 2026-03-09 16:05 (115 minutes), plus a second blip 2026-03-12 11:30 to 12:20 (50 minutes). Total 165 minutes this quarter.

ben_engineer: Got it. Quick calc script I use: ```python
# inputs: monthly_fee_usd, outage_minutes, days_in_month
credit = min(0.1 * monthly_fee_usd, (outage_minutes / (days_in_month*24*60)) * monthly_fee_usd)
print(credit)
```

ben_engineer: Using that, for $45,000 monthly and a 30-day month: outage_fraction = 165 / (30*24*60) ~= 0.00383 -> credit ~= $172. That is well under the playbook cap (10% -> $4,500).

jess_sales: OK that's small relative to renewal. We should still offer it + a short technical note and an invite to a remediation walkthrough. Avoid legal language, make it proactive.

laura_onboard: I'll schedule a 30-min enablement + remediation walk for next week and attach onboarding docs we updated last month. ETA: invite by EOD tomorrow.

maya_success: Can we draft the customer email here? I'd propose: 1) acknowledge 2) explain root cause (model rollout + autoscale lag) 3) offer credit $172 + invite for remediation call 4) outline steps we've taken. Short, empathetic.

elaine_cs: Drafted quick copy below — please edit. "Hi team — thanks for flagging latency last week. We traced this to a model rollout which temporarily caused autoscale lag. We've deployed an autoscale fix, added warm-pool safeguards, and will monitor. As a small goodwill gesture we've issued a credit of $172 to your account; we'd like to walk through the remediation plan on a short call. Please pick a time here: <calendar link>."

jess_sales: I trimmed it slightly and added renewal-context sentence. Approved from sales side.

raj_reliability: Actionables from my end: add warm-pool health check, push canary gating for model rollouts, add an alert if scale doesn't meet target within 2m. I'll have PR by EOD.

ben_engineer: I'll drop the credit line item into billing (ticket BILL-889) and attach calculation. ETA 1 business day.

laura_onboard: Invite sent to customer, remediation walkthrough scheduled for 2026-03-18 16:00 PT.

maya_success: I'll own the customer follow-up after the call; capture feedback and update the account health playbook.

elaine_cs: Thanks all. Quick checklist: (1) billing credit (Ben) — 1d, (2) PR for autoscale hardening (Raj) — EOD, (3) invite & docs (Laura) — sent, (4) CS follow-up + playbook update (Maya) — post-call. If anything else needed ping me. :thumbsup:
